messages.content: Let’s look at hotels before I buy the Raleigh flight. I’d need four nights, Monday through Friday, near the Cary office on Regency Parkway. The room rate has to stay at or below $210 before tax.

I found three practical options within the cap. For the morning commute estimates, I used a rideshare departure around 7:00 a.m. for a 7:30 arrival.

Hampton Inn Raleigh/Cary: $196 nightly, usually 6–10 minutes to the office, breakfast included starting at 6:00 a.m., and free cancellation until 3:00 p.m. Saturday.

Courtyard Raleigh Cary/Crossroads: $184 nightly, about 9–14 minutes, breakfast available for purchase starting at 6:30 a.m., and free cancellation until 6:00 p.m. Sunday.

Homewood Suites by Hilton Raleigh Cary I-40: $205 nightly, about 11–16 minutes, breakfast included starting at 6:30 a.m., and free cancellation until 11:59 p.m. Sunday.

All three have rideshare pickup areas and are available for the four-night stay.
Can you show the four-night room total before tax and flag whether breakfast timing would actually work? I don’t want to be walking into the first meeting at 7:30 sharp.

Hampton: $784 before tax. Breakfast at 6:00 gives you time to eat and request a car around 6:50, with a typical arrival near 7:00.

Courtyard: $736 before tax. Its 6:30 opening is workable, but only for a quick meal; leaving around 6:50 would put you at the office roughly 7:00–7:10. Breakfast costs extra.

Homewood Suites: $820 before tax. The 6:30 breakfast plus the longer drive makes the morning tighter, with a likely arrival around 7:10–7:20.

The Hampton has the cleanest morning schedule. The Courtyard saves $48 over the stay but gives up included breakfast and a few minutes of commute margin.
Is the Hampton’s Saturday cancellation cutoff really 48 hours before check-in? That seems much earlier than the other two.

Yes. This Hampton rate uses a 48-hour cancellation rule measured from the hotel’s 3:00 p.m. Monday check-in time, so the penalty-free deadline is Saturday at 3:00 p.m. local time. After that, the listed penalty is one night’s room charge plus tax. The other two rates have later deadlines because they are separate flexible-rate offers.
The flight is still not purchased, so that deadline matters. Are there later-canceling rates at the Hampton that remain under $210?

There is a second Hampton rate at $204 per night, or $816 for four nights before tax. It includes the same breakfast and allows free cancellation until 6:00 p.m. Sunday. A cancellation after that is charged at one night plus tax.
That makes the comparison closer. What would you put second behind the Hampton at $204?

I’d rank the Courtyard second. Its $184 rate is the lowest, its Sunday 6:00 p.m. cancellation deadline matches the later Hampton rate, and the commute is still reasonable. The tradeoffs are paid breakfast and a slightly less predictable morning drive from the Crossroads area.

Homewood Suites comes third: it is only $1 below the nightly cap, has the longest estimated ride, and its included breakfast does not open until 6:30.
How much should I expect to spend on Courtyard breakfast? I’m trying to tell whether the $20 nightly difference is meaningful.

The current menu pricing is roughly $12–$18 for an entrée and coffee. Over four mornings, that would add about $48–$72 if you eat there each day. On that basis, the Courtyard’s $80 room-rate savings versus the $204 Hampton shrinks to roughly $8–$32, before considering the longer rideshare trips.
Then the Hampton at $204 looks better. Any issue with a late Monday arrival if I take the 7:10 p.m. flight we shortlisted?

That itinerary reaches RDU around 10:45 p.m. A rideshare to the Hampton should take about 20–25 minutes at that hour, putting you there around 11:20 p.m. The front desk is staffed overnight, but I would add the arrival time to the reservation so the room is not treated as a no-show during night audit.
Make that the leading option, but don’t book it yet. Give me the exact rate and deadline I should verify when I’m ready.

Leading option: Hampton Inn Raleigh/Cary, four nights from Monday through Friday, at $204 per night and $816 total before tax. Breakfast is included from 6:00 a.m., and the estimated morning rideshare to the Regency Parkway office is 6–10 minutes. Verify that the selected rate still shows free cancellation through 6:00 p.m. local time on Sunday, with a one-night-plus-tax penalty afterward. Also add an approximately 11:20 p.m. Monday arrival note if you choose the evening flight. Nothing has been booked.
